title: Stabilizer invariants of transitive domain products and their fraction fields
statement: Let $H$ be a finite group acting transitively on a nonempty finite set $I$. For each $i\in I$, let $B_i$ be a commutative integral domain (a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors). Suppose ring isomorphisms $\rho_{h,i}:B_i\to B_{hi}$ satisfy $\rho_{1,i}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{gh,i}=\rho_{g,hi}\circ\rho_{h,i}$. Equip $B=\prod_{i\in I}B_i$ with the action characterized by $(hb)_{hi}=\rho_{h,i}(b_i)$, and write $B^H=\{b\in B:hb=b\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Fix $i\in I$ and set $D=\{h\in H:hi=i\}$ and $B_i^D=\{a\in B_i:\rho_{h,i}(a)=a\text{ for all }h\in D\}$. Projection $p_i:B\to B_i$ restricts to a ring isomorphism $B^H\cong B_i^D$. More generally, if $A$ is a commutative ring and $u:A\to B$ is an injective unital ring homomorphism with image $B^H$, then $A$ is a domain, $a_i=p_i\circ u$ is injective with image $B_i^D$, and its unique fraction-field extension [def-pc-field-extension] has image $\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)^D$. Here $\operatorname{Frac}R$ is the field of quotients of a domain $R$ under its canonical injection, and the action of $D$ on $\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)$ is $h(b/c)=\rho_{h,i}(b)/\rho_{h,i}(c)$. No faithfulness, characteristic assumption, normality of $D$ in $H$, or invertibility of $|H|$ is required.

proof.text: For $h\in H$ define $\alpha_h:B\to B$ by $(\alpha_h(b))_{hj}=\rho_{h,j}(b_j)$ for all $j\in I$; this is the action of the statement. Each $\alpha_h$ is a unital ring homomorphism, being coordinatewise given by the ring maps $\rho_{h,j}$ after the bijection $j\mapsto hj$. The cocycle identities give $\alpha_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_{gh}=\alpha_g\alpha_h$, so each $\alpha_h$ is an automorphism with inverse $\alpha_{h^{-1}}$. Since $\rho_{h,j}(1)=1$ and $\rho_{h,j}(0)=0$, the coordinate idempotents $e_j\in B$ (coordinate $1$ at $j$, $0$ elsewhere) satisfy $\alpha_h(e_j)=e_{hj}$. Hence the unique action on $I$ in [lem-sfb-domain-product-action-fixed-ring] is the given action, and the unique isomorphisms $h_j$ there are $\rho_{h,j}$, because both satisfy $(\alpha_h(x))_{hj}=h_j(x_j)$ for all $x$. Thus its $H_i$ is $D$, its $C_i$ is $B_i^D$, and its $B^H$ is the $B^H$ of the statement.

proof.text: By transitivity, $R=\{i\}$ contains exactly one representative of the single orbit $I$. Apply [lem-sfb-domain-product-action-fixed-ring] with this $R$, using the identifications of the preceding step. It gives that projection $e=p_i|_{B^H}:B^H\to B_i^D$ is a ring isomorphism, with inverse $a\mapsto(\rho_{h,i}(a))_{hi}$, independent of the choice of $h$. This is the first assertion of the statement.

proof.text: Under the hypothesis on $u$, its corestriction $A\to B^H$ is bijective. Composing with $e$ shows that $a_i$ is injective and has image $B_i^D$. Also $1_A\ne0_A$, since $a_i$ is unital and $B_i$ is nonzero. If $ab=0$ in $A$, then $a_i(a)a_i(b)=0$ in the domain $B_i$; one factor is zero, and injectivity gives $a=0$ or $b=0$. This proves that $A$ is a domain, without claiming that the product $B$ is a domain.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation for the constant finite action groupoid, contextualizing Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), part (3); the coordinate calculation is written here, not asserted to be the statement of that tag.

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift] to the injective map $A\xrightarrow{a_i}B_i\hookrightarrow L$. It gives the unique injective extension $v:K\to L$, with $v(a/c)=a_i(a)/a_i(c)$. For $d\in D$, apply the same node to $B_i\xrightarrow{\rho_{d,i}}B_i\hookrightarrow L$. The resulting map on $L$ is $b/c\mapsto\rho_{d,i}(b)/\rho_{d,i}(c)$. Its inverse is the map for $d^{-1}$, and the identity and composition laws follow by uniqueness, since they hold on $B_i$. Thus these maps are an action on $L$ by ring automorphisms.

source.place: Fraction-field universal property as recorded by lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift (Tag 0BI0, lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain, quotient embedding); uniqueness and formula are the cited node statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-invariant-fraction-field-lifting] with $G=D$, $R=A$, $S=B_i$, $f=a_i$, and the fraction fields and map $v$ just constructed. The group $D$ is finite because it is a subgroup of finite $H$; step 4 gives the required injectivity and image equality. The leaf gives $L^D\subseteq\operatorname{im}(v)$. Conversely, each $v(a/c)=a_i(a)/a_i(c)$ is fixed by every $d\in D$, since both numerator and denominator lie in $B_i^D$. Therefore $\operatorname{im}(v)=L^D$. All calculations use only automorphisms, transitivity and finiteness, with no division by a group order.

lean.statement: theorem transitive_domain_product_invariants (H : Type u) [Group H] [Finite H] (I : Type v) [Finite I] [Nonempty I] [MulAction H I] (htrans : ∀ i j : I, ∃ h : H, h • i = j) (B : I → Type w) [∀ i : I, CommRing (B i)] [∀ i : I, IsDomain (B i)] (ρ : ∀ (h : H) (i : I), B i ≃+* B (h • i)) (hρone : ∀ i : I, (ρ 1 i).trans (RingEquiv.cast (R := B) (one_smul H i)) = RingEquiv.refl (B i)) (hρmul : ∀ (g h : H) (i : I), (ρ (g * h) i).trans (RingEquiv.cast (R := B) (mul_smul g h i)) = (ρ h i).trans (ρ g (h • i))) (i : I) : (∃ e : transitiveProductFixedSubring B ρ ≃+* transitiveStabilizerFixedSubring B ρ i, ∀ b : transitiveProductFixedSubring B ρ, (e b : B i) = (b : ∀ j : I, B j) i) ∧ (∀ (A : Type a) [CommRing A] (f : A →+* (∀ j : I, B j)), Function.Injective f → f.range = transitiveProductFixedSubring B ρ → IsDomain A ∧ Function.Injective ((Pi.evalRingHom B i).comp f) ∧ ((Pi.evalRingHom B i).comp f).range = transitiveStabilizerFixedSubring B ρ i ∧ ∀ (K : Type k) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (L : Type l) [Field L] [Algebra (B i) L] [IsFractionRing (B i) L], ∃ v : K →+* L, v.comp (algebraMap A K) = (algebraMap (B i) L).comp ((Pi.evalRingHom B i).comp f) ∧ (∀ v' : K →+* L, v'.comp (algebraMap A K) = (algebraMap (B i) L).comp ((Pi.evalRingHom B i).comp f) → v' = v) ∧ Set.range v = {x : L | ∀ (h : H) (hi : h • i = i), IsFractionRing.ringEquivOfRingEquiv (K := L) (L := L) ((ρ h i).trans (RingEquiv.cast (R := B) hi)) x = x})
